summary.one_liner: Concourse is an open-source automation system written in Go, most commonly used for CI/CD pipelines, configured with declarative YAML.
summary.what_it_does: Concourse is an automation system written in Go and most commonly used for CI/CD, though it is described as scalable to any kind of automation pipeline. The README says it is opinionated about idempotency, immutability, declarative config, stateless workers, and reproducible builds. It is distributed as a single concourse binary, with a Docker image, Kubernetes Helm chart, and BOSH release also supported. Pipelines are defined in declarative YAML files rather than through a GUI, and are managed mostly with the fly CLI (for example, fly set-pipeline). The README's quick start uses docker-compose to run a local instance with a test/test login, and points to a web UI for downloading fly.
use_cases: automating tasks triggered by git changes
defining reproducible build pipelines in YAML
how_to_run: wget the repository's docker-compose file (URL not included in the README text)
Log in with fly -t ci login -c <url> -u test -p test
Write a pipeline YAML file with resources and jobs
notable: Pipelines are declarative YAML with no GUI configuration step
Workers are stateless and builds aim to be reproducible
Ships as a single binary plus Docker, Helm, and BOSH options
Includes a fly CLI for setting and running pipelines
caveats: README does not state a license
Quick start download URLs are missing from the provided README text
Installation details for non-Docker formats are deferred to other repositories
